A_target.statement:
Let $V$ be an [[Definition:Inner Product Space|inner product space]] and $v_1, \ldots, v_n$ [[Definition:Linearly Independent Set|linearly independent]].
Then there exist [[Definition:Orthonormal Subset|orthonormal]] $q_1, \ldots, q_n$ such that for each $k$:
:$\map {\operatorname {span} } {q_1, \ldots, q_k} = \map {\operatorname {span} } {v_1, \ldots, v_k}$

B_source.statement:
Let $U$ be a finite-dimensional [[Definition:Vector Subspace|subspace]] of an [[Definition:Inner Product Space|inner product space]] $V$.
Then every $v \in V$ decomposes as:
:$v = \map {\operatorname {proj}_U} v + \paren {v - \map {\operatorname {proj}_U} v}$
with $v - \map {\operatorname {proj}_U} v \perp U$.

substitutions.the subspace U: the span of already-processed vectors q_1,...,q_{k-1}
substitutions.the orthogonal remainder v - proj_U(v): the new orthogonal direction before normalizing

derived.orthogonality of the remainder to U: orthogonality of q_k to all earlier q_i

object_map.reformulation: Apply the single-step projection decomposition repeatedly, each time projecting onto the span of the vectors already orthonormalized.

validity_conditions: At step k, subtracting the projection onto span(q_1,...,q_{k-1}) leaves a vector orthogonal to all earlier q_i (the defining property of orthogonal projection).
The v_i are linearly independent, so each remainder is nonzero and can be normalized.
Iterating preserves the spanning flag: span(q_1..q_k) = span(v_1..v_k).
